Priya to schedule deep-dive with Horizon network team to walk through Transit Gateway and peering options (by 2026-09-29)

meeting_header: Date: 2026-09-22 | Time: 16:00-16:45 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Lane (Horizon CTO), Aisha Khan (Horizon Head of Platform), Leo Park (Horizon Network Engineer)
summary: Discovery focused on Horizon's requirements for a Private VPC deployment: cross-region constraints, VPC peering vs Transit Gateway, private endpoints (PrivateLink), network egress/ingress controls, KMS integration, and compliance needs. Agreed to share network runbook and set up a technical deep-dive with Horizon's networking team.
topics: Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Audit logs, SOC2 and SSO integration
transcript:
00:00 Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, with Priya our SE. Quick intro, and then we'll dive into the VPC and networking stuff.
00:12 Marcus: Hey Jordan, thanks. Marcus here, CTO at Horizon Dynamics. We've got Aisha and Leo on. We're evaluating options — hosted, dedicated, or private — but for regulatory reasons we think Private VPC is the way.
00:28 Priya: Great, and just so I set context, Private means customer-managed VPC with our control plane split, right? We can run the inference runtime inside your VPC or connect via private endpoints depending on the pattern you want.
00:38 Aisha: Correct. Our security team is pretty strict: data must not traverse public internet, keys must be under our KMS, and we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also region placement matters — some workloads must stay in eu-west-1 and us-east-1.
00:56 Priya: Makes sense. A couple of common patterns: 1) Full Private deployment where Redwood ships a package into your VPC (dedicated nodes inside your subnets) and we only present an internal endpoint, or 2) Private endpoints pattern where our control plane is hosted but traffic goes over PrivateLink/Interface endpoints. Each has different networking requirements.
01:18 Leo: Quick Q — when you say "ships a package" do you mean like an AMI or container image? What's the network footprint? We run EKS and have strict egress rules.
01:27 Priya: Usually containers in your cluster or private EC2/ECS. Network-wise the runtime needs outbound access to pull models initially (we can ship models via signed objects or airgap), and then it listens on private subnets. For management/control plane we either peer or use VPC endpoints to avoid public IPs.
01:46 Marcus: We prefer not to peer directly across our prod VPCs. Transit Gateway is our standard for shared services. Does Redwood support Transit Gateway attachments?
01:55 Jordan: Yes, we commonly attach to TGW — we can request a TGW attachment from the customer side. For very large orgs we do TGW or PrivateLink based on routing controls. There are some limits and routing table work, we'll share best practices.
02:10 Leo: And inter-region? We have nodes in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. VPC peering cross-region is possible but we prefer TGW for centralization. Any latency implications?
02:20 Priya: TGW cross-region works, but there's inter-region latency — typically a few tens of ms depending on path. For low-latency inference we recommend placing inference nodes in the same region as the request origin. If you need multi-region failover, we can support active-passive with sync of model artifacts to regional deployments.
02:38 Aisha: How do you handle auth between our VPC and Redwood's control plane? We need SAML SSO for console and mTLS for service-to-service, plus we want to integrate with our KMS.
02:49 Jordan: For console/ops SSO we support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning. For service auth we do mutual TLS and token-based service auth. KMS — we can integrate with customer-managed keys (CMKs) for disk encryption and for model artifact encryption in transit and at rest. For HSM-level requirements we have partners and on-prem options.
03:08 Marcus: Re: audit logs, does Redwood push logs to our S3 or do we pull? SIEM integration?
03:14 Priya: We can forward audit logs to your S3 bucket or to a syslog endpoint; common pattern is Kinesis Firehose to S3, then your SIEM. We also support pushing to a customer-owned CloudWatch account via cross-account role so logs never leave your org.
03:30 Leo: Network nitty-gritty — what ports/protocols? Security groups?
03:34 Priya: We'll provide a network runbook. High-level: service-to-service TCP on 443 for HTTPS, some gRPC ports for telemetry if enabled, and ephemeral ports for container orchestration. Security groups should allow our subnets to talk to model-serving subnets and to the ECR/S3 endpoints for image/artifact pulls. We'll enumerate CIDR blocks and FQDNs.
03:55 Marcus: We use strict NAT gateways for outbound. Will your runtime need internet egress for model downloads and occasional heartbeat? If so we need to route via our NAT and monitor.
04:05 Priya: Yes, initial model acquisition often requires outbound. But once models are pre-staged inside your environment we can lock it down. Heartbeats can be proxied over PrivateLink to our control plane if you prefer.
04:18 Jordan: I want to surface a couple practical caveats we've seen: 1) VPC peering can get messy at scale because route tables multiply; 2) if you need cross-account peering with many accounts, Transit Gateway or PrivateLink becomes simpler; 3) inter-region peering has replication overhead for models.
04:36 Aisha: Understood. For compliance we also need data residency controls and the ability to pin model versions so that inference uses only approved weights. Is that possible?
04:46 Priya: Absolutely — you can pin model versions and we support an allowlist of models for a deployment. Model artifacts are stored in your S3 under your account for Private deployments, so residency is enforced by your region choice.
04:58 Leo: A practical question: routing tables and overlapping CIDR ranges are a pain for us. What do you need?
05:04 Priya: We'll ask for non-overlapping subnets for the Redwood-managed subnets. If overlap exists we can NAT/proxy but it's complicated. We'll provide sample CIDR ranges and a template CloudFormation / ARM / Terraform to standardize.
05:18 Marcus: Does Redwood require any ingress from the internet for health checks or updates?
05:24 Priya: No public ingress is required. We operate over private endpoints. For control-plane callbacks you can require the TGW or PrivateLink. There is an optional inbound for support sessions if you enable support access — but that's toggleable and audited.
05:38 Aisha: Encryption at rest — can we use our CMKs for EBS/EFS and for any object storage you use?
05:45 Priya: Yes, you control the keys. We will request IAM roles to allow Redwood-managed instances to use the key for EBS/EFS or KMS encrypt/decrypt of model objects; you maintain key lifecycle.
05:55 Leo: Any specific IAM permissions needed? We run least privilege so we need a list to create roles.
06:00 Priya: We'll provide a least-privilege role manifest. Broadly: S3 get/put for bucket prefix, ECR pull if we use ECR, CloudWatch put metrics/logs, and KMS: Encrypt/Decrypt permissions on the CMK. We'll send the exact policy.
06:12 Jordan: Quick note on Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated is Redwood-managed but single-tenant pools we host — network is simpler, but data traverses Redwood's network (not suitable if you need all data in your VPC). Private is customer-controlled and meets stricter compliance.
06:27 Marcus: Cost wise, what's the delta? We need ballpark to evaluate.
06:31 Jordan: Private has higher setup and operational overhead for you but less per-token egress billing to Redwood; Dedicated sits in middle, hosted is cheapest ops for you but higher trust boundary. I'll send an initial pricing sheet after the call.
06:45 Aisha: Regarding region constraints: we have EU-only workloads. Can you run entirely in eu-west-1 with no fallback to US?
06:52 Priya: Yes. For Private we deploy into your eu-west-1 and nothing leaves that region unless you configure cross-region replication. Our control plane can be regionally colocated or you can choose private control plane options.
07:06 Leo: What's the deployment time like — from sign to running inference in our VPC?
07:11 Jordan: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: network setup and cert exchange 1 week, model staging and validation 1 week, performance tuning another week. For air-gapped/on-prem it can be longer.
07:24 Marcus: Ok. On networking specifics: do you recommend PrivateLink over TGW? We have a hub-and-spoke with TGW.
07:32 Priya: For hub-and-spoke TGW usually fits best. PrivateLink is good when you want service isolation and minimal route table changes, and you want to expose a single service endpoint per region. TGW simplifies many spokes with central routing and is easier when you have many accounts. We'll align to whatever your networking org prefers.
07:51 Leo: One more thing — our security folks want mTLS pinned to certs issued by our internal CA. Can Redwood accept customer-supplied certs for service-to-service?
07:59 Priya: We can support mTLS with customer certs in Private deployments. We'll need to integrate with your PKI and agree on rotation processes. It's doable but requires ops coordination.
08:12 Marcus: Do you have a security whitepaper and SOC2 cert we can share with compliance?
08:16 Jordan: Yes we do. I'll attach SOC2 report and our security whitepaper; for Private deployments we'll also include the runbook with network diagrams and IAM policies.
08:27 Aisha: Any known limits on throughput for private deployments? We expect bursts for real-time inference.
08:33 Priya: Throughput depends on node sizing and GPU types. We can size Dedicated/Private clusters to meet your QPS and latency SLO. For bursts, we can configure autoscaling or burst capacity, but that requires capacity planning. We'll run a small benchmark during the pilot.
08:48 Leo: If we do cross-region failover, how do you keep KV cache/contexts consistent?
08:53 Priya: We generally don't sync KV cache across regions; it's local for latency. For session handoff we recommend stateless request contexts or store contexts in a customer-managed store (e.g., DynamoDB globally replicated) rather than relying on cross-region KV.
09:10 Marcus: That makes sense. Can we do a short proof-of-concept next month? We want performance numbers and a security review.
09:17 Jordan: Absolutely. Next steps we'll: share network runbook, schedule a deep-dive for the network team, send pricing and pilot checklist.
09:26 Aisha: Also want to loop in our procurement for contracts timeline — we aim to have vendor selected by mid-October.
09:32 Jordan: Got it. We'll move quickly.
09:36 Priya: Any other questions about tooling or integrations, like model registry or deployment pinning?
09:41 Marcus: Not at the moment. We'll review the runbook and follow up.
09:45 Jordan: Cool, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and set the deep-dive.
09:49 [END]
